newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative launches anti-EMU book.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative launches anti-EMU book.

text.p: Leading Conservative politician John Redwood on Wednesday launched a book attacking a single European currency but denied that he was at odds with colleagues in Britain's ruling party.

Redwood, a right-wing Eurosceptic who challenged Prime Minister John Major for leadership of the Conservative Party in 1995, launched his book -- "Our Currency, Our Country" -- with little fanfare in a London bookshop.
"A single currency on the fudged basis currently on offer would be extremely damaging for Britain," he told reporters. "It would mean lost jobs and higher taxation."
"What this books says is that it is very unlikely there will be anything on offer except a fudged single currency."

Eurosceptics argue that European economic and monetary union (EMU) is being rammed through for political reasons, before European Union economies have converged sufficiently. The pressures of moulding those economies into the shape required for EMU and keeping them there will lead to unbearable pressures which will rip the system apart, they argue.
At the launch, Redwood fielded questions from a 20-strong press pack but it looked as if only one customer stepped forward to buy a signed copy of the book.

Redwood said he agreed with the government's "wait and see" position to remain at the negotiation table to change the European Union's plans for the better or convince Britain's partners that a single currency would be disastrous.

"I respect the government's position, they have difficult negotiations ahead. But I wish to make out the case that when they come to decide they must say no," Redwood said. That, he said, meant he was "singing from a very similar hymn sheet to the Chancellor".
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke is widely seen as the most pro-European member of the Conservative government.
But even he has said the single currency is unlikely to go ahead on its scheduled start date of January 1, 1999.
Redwood denied he had been "lent on" by senior Conservatives to cancel a full-blown press launch for his book.
With a May 1 election approaching fast and the Conservatives still 20 points and more behind in the polls, campaign managers will not welcome any signs of division over Europe.
Last week, Tory Chairman Brian Mawhinney advised party members that if they had nothing helpful to say, they should say nothing.

Redwood pledged to fight hard for the Conservative Party through the election campaign but asked if he thought they would win, he appeared to be less than bullish. "I never prophesy Conservative defeats," he said.
